content.text:
## Core pitch

**QuoteCraft turns a fragmented RFQ into a traceable, correctly priced, signed bid—without hardcoded portal paths or tender values.**

“Manufacturers do not receive all bid information in one place. The RFQ may be in a tender portal, specifications and supplier data elsewhere, stock and price scales in ERP, and approvals or signing codes in email. QuoteCraft coordinates four model-directed agents—one per system—to gather only relevant evidence. It converts that evidence into a shared, structured case file, then applies the commercial rules with deterministic Decimal arithmetic. Finally, a portal agent enters the bid, retrieves a fresh TAN from mail, checks the live review page, and submits only after the portal shows a valid bid.”

```text
Tender brief
   ↓
4 parallel site agents → evidence + provenance → shared case file
   ↓
Exact commercial calculator
   ↓
Portal clerk → live review gate → TAN from mail → submitted receipt
```

The key differentiator: **the LLM decides what to inspect and how to navigate unfamiliar websites; deterministic code handles money, validation, and irreversible-submit safeguards.** This makes it agentic but commercially reliable.

## How we submit the bid

For this challenge, the platform supplies a run contract: the brief, site access, credentials, deadline, and whether the target is a website or API. We do not assume the submission method. [run.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/run.py:31)

1. We reserve up to eight minutes (or 40% of the run) for form completion and signing rather than researching until time expires. [agent.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/agent.py:286)

2. The research agents file evidence from the tender portal, supplier portal, ERP, and mailbox. The calculator creates the final bid sheet: offered material, quantities, unit prices, lead times, discount, total, and any legitimately omitted positions. [agent.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/agent.py:324) · [calculator.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/calculator.py:264)

3. When the run says `submission.kind = "site"`, we submit directly in the tender website—not by merely returning JSON. A fresh model-directed “bid clerk” reads the form and enters the bid sheet according to whatever layout it finds. [agent.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/agent.py:345) · [submit.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/submit.py:172)

4. If the portal requires a TAN, the clerk requests it only after triggering the portal request. A second agent searches the mailbox for the newest matching code, avoiding stale or decoy codes. [submit.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/submit.py:232)

5. Immediately before the irreversible click, a deterministic preflight check verifies visible portal errors, empty required fields, tender reference, offered positions, and the calculated total. The final button can only be pressed through `finalize` after that check. [submit.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/submit.py:275) · [preflight.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/preflight.py:41)

6. After the final click, code—not another model call—reads the confirmation/receipt, because the run token may expire immediately after submission. For API-type tasks, there is a separate authenticated JSON submission path. [submit.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/submit.py:280) · [run.py](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/run.py:72)

## Good jury answers

**“Why is this genuinely agentic?”**  
We do not script URLs, selectors, click paths, tender IDs, or prices. The model decides where to search, which document is evidence, and how to complete the unfamiliar form. The code only provides safe generic browser tools and exact calculations.

**“How do you avoid hallucinated commercial decisions?”**  
Only filed source evidence enters the case file. The calculator uses `Decimal` rounding and explicit tender rules; unknown values are not invented. The review gate checks what the portal visibly holds before submission.

**“Why four browsers?”**  
They mirror the real information silos—tender, supplier, ERP, and mail—and investigate in parallel. We stay exactly within the challenge’s four-browser maximum. [agent.json](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/starter-kit/agent.json:4)

**“What happens if a position cannot be priced?”**  
We do not fabricate it. The agent uses the portal’s explicit omission flow where available, then signs the valid bid for the positions supported by evidence.

**“Does it work on the private dataset?”**  
That is the design goal: page access is rendered as generic accessible text, not tied to known HTML or portal paths. Different layouts require the model to reason at runtime.

## What not to overclaim

Say that the architecture and unit-tested submission safeguards are implemented. Do **not** claim a confirmed official 100/100 or final live submission until the official end-to-end run has produced a portal receipt; the current status document explicitly marks that validation as pending. [PROJECT_STATUS.md](D:/Personal_Projects/TUM_HackathonFinal/PROJECT_STATUS.md:4)

For a demo, show: one site observation → filed evidence/case file → calculated bid → live review checklist → TAN retrieval → receipt.

> “QuoteCraft is a bounded-autonomy, multi-agent, neuro-symbolic workflow for RFQ-to-bid automation.”

## Your technical story

“We are not building a traditional scraper or a chatbot that guesses prices. QuoteCraft is a **tool-grounded multi-agent system**. Four specialized browser agents investigate separate enterprise systems in parallel: tender portal, supplier portal, ERP, and email.

Each agent works through an **accessibility-grounded action space**: the browser is converted into structured, screen-reader-style text with numbered controls. The model chooses the next navigation, search, document, or form action at runtime. That means we do not hardcode CSS selectors, URLs, click paths, tender references, or prices.

The agents coordinate through a **shared blackboard architecture**—our provenance-aware case file. Every relevant page is converted into a typed intermediate representation: tender positions, technical requirements, material records, price conditions, approvals, and mail evidence. New evidence automatically generates the next open research question for the appropriate specialist.

The core is **neuro-symbolic**: the LLM handles perception, navigation, document selection, and workflow adaptation; deterministic code handles Decimal arithmetic, tender rules, rounding, eligibility checks, and commercial constraints. We intentionally separate probabilistic reasoning from financial truth.

Finally, bid submission is a **policy-gated irreversible-action workflow**. The portal agent fills the dynamic form, a mail courier retrieves the latest TAN, and a deterministic preflight gate checks visible errors, required fields, reference, positions, and total before the final submit action is allowed. The confirmation receipt is captured as evidence.”

## Fancy terms that are accurate

| Say this | What it means in our project |
|---|---|
| **Tool-grounded agents** | The model acts through controlled browser tools, not free-form browser scripting. |
| **Accessibility-grounded perception** | Pages become accessible text plus numbered controls, including frames, tooltips, dialogs, and collapsed sections. |
| **Role-specialized multi-agent orchestration** | Separate agents handle tender, supplier, ERP, and mail systems. |
| **Shared blackboard architecture** | The case file is the shared source of truth; agents react to newly derived open questions. |
| **Provenance-aware evidence ledger** | Filed facts retain their source URL, document identity, site agent, and merge result. |
| **Typed intermediate representation** | Pages become structured positions, requirements, materials, conditions, approvals, and messages. |
| **Hybrid neuro-symbolic reasoning** | LLM for discovery/navigation; deterministic `Decimal` rules for commercial calculations. |
| **Closed-loop browser control** | Actions are followed by state checks; stale controls, failed loads, and loops trigger recovery. |
| **Bounded autonomy** | Four-browser cap, time budgets, step limits, constrained JSON actions, and guarded finalization. |
| **Policy-gated finalization** | A deterministic preflight must approve before an irreversible submit click. |

## Important contrast line

> “This is live, agentic retrieval—not classical vector-database RAG. The evidence is discovered from active enterprise portals during the run, then converted into validated structured facts.”

Do not claim a vector database, embeddings, an event-sourced system, or a graph database—we do not need them, and the jury may ask.

## Submission explanation, in technical language

> “Submission is not an API mock. For site-based challenge runs, our orchestration layer hands the deterministic bid sheet to a portal clerk agent. It interprets the unseen form at runtime, enters the exact values, requests a signing TAN, delegates TAN retrieval to a mailbox courier, executes a preflight verification pass, and only then invokes the guarded finalization action. After that irreversible click, code captures the portal receipt directly, because the challenge token can expire immediately after submission.”

## Strong answers to likely technical questions

**Why multi-agent instead of one agent?**  
“Enterprise evidence is naturally distributed across systems. Role specialization reduces context overload and lets us run parallel investigation while synchronizing through a shared evidence ledger.”

**How do you prevent hallucinations?**  
“The model never becomes the calculator. It can only contribute filed evidence; exact commercial decisions are deterministic and every final portal submission has a live-page verification gate.”

**How do you generalize to the private dataset?**  
“We avoid portal-specific selectors and paths. The agent reads the visible accessible interface and decides actions dynamically, so the adaptation happens at runtime rather than through public-scenario hardcoding.”

**What makes it safe?**  
“Defense in depth: typed extraction, provenance, decimal arithmetic, loop detection, tab recovery, bounded time, single-use TAN handling, and a zero-trust final-submit gate.”

**What is your innovation in one line?**  
> “We turn autonomous browsing into an auditable commercial workflow by combining agentic retrieval with deterministic financial reasoning and verified portal execution.”
